title: Internal Technical Knowledge & Research Base
description: I created and maintained a private internal technical knowledge base for Essential Skills using WordPress on AWS. I used it to continuously research emerging development practices, languages, frameworks and infrastructure technologies, document what I learned, evaluate whether those technologies were appropriate for our production systems, and then transfer that knowledge to the other developers and support staff.

sections.title: Continuous Technical Research
paragraphs: A major purpose of the knowledge base was to keep our development practices current as web and software technologies changed.

I would research and learn unfamiliar technologies first, document what I discovered, evaluate whether they made sense for Essential Skills, and then teach or introduce the useful concepts to the rest of the development team.

sections.title: Research Topics
paragraphs: The knowledge base accumulated research and technical documentation across the technologies and architectural approaches we were evaluating at the time.

sections.title: Internal Knowledge Sharing
paragraphs: The site was used by both the development team and support staff.
I authored most of the material. Other employees would occasionally find useful information or resources and pass them to me to evaluate and add to the knowledge base.

sections.title: Documentation Platform
paragraphs: I configured WordPress as an internal technical documentation system rather than as a conventional public blog.

sections.title: Infrastructure & Administration
paragraphs: I provisioned and administered the underlying AWS/Linux environment in addition to configuring WordPress itself.

sections.title: Private Internal Access
paragraphs: The knowledge base was kept private for internal company use.
The exact access-control configuration is no longer certain; during this period I used approaches including application authentication and restricting EC2 services to company IP addresses.

sections.title: Active Research Period
paragraphs: During its active period I added research and documentation frequently, often adding material daily for months.
Use declined later as the company development team became smaller and the need for a shared internal research library decreased.

sections.title: Learning Before Leading
paragraphs: The knowledge base reflected my normal approach to technical leadership: learn and test a technology myself before deciding whether it should enter the production stack or teaching it to other developers.

historicalNotes: The legacy portfolio card was titled simply 'Wordpress', but WordPress was the implementation technology rather than the primary purpose of the project.
The system was an internal Essential Skills technical knowledge base and research library.
Jamie authored most of the material; coworkers occasionally supplied useful material for Jamie to review and add.
Primary users included developers and support staff.
Jamie provisioned and administered the EC2/Ubuntu, web-server, PHP, MySQL and WordPress environment.
Jamie does not remember whether this particular installation used Apache or NGINX, so neither web server should be claimed specifically on the public card.
Jamie separately configured another WordPress server environment for an outside company that converted Essential Skills' main Drupal website to WordPress.
Jamie did not create the preceding Drupal storefront.
Jamie had stopped being the primary developer of the Essential Skills public storefront after the earlier ASP.NET generation.
The knowledge base was private. Exact access control is uncertain; it may have used WordPress authentication or EC2/network access restricted to the Essential Skills business IP.
Jamie added documentation frequently, often daily for months during the active period.
The site eventually fell out of use as the company development team became smaller due to financial constraints.
